title: Deployment Permit
description: The human-signed, time-bounded authority to operate. Bound to a specific Passport digest, which is the point: a permit for one configuration cannot silently be applied to a modified agent. Renewal after a change issues a NEW permit bound to the new Passport rather than mutating this one, so the register always shows what was authorised at any past moment. A permit does not certify an agent as safe; it states precisely what it may do and under what conditions.

passport_digest.description: Configuration fingerprint this authority is bound to.

state.description: Where the permit is in its life. Deliberately distinct from level: a suspended production permit and a suspended evaluation permit are different facts, and collapsing them loses the agent's approved boundary.

conditions.description: Named controls the approval depends on. Losing one restricts the permit.

suspension_triggers.description: Material change kinds that suspend this permit automatically.

restricted_to_boundary.description: When restricted rather than suspended, the boundary the PREVIOUS evidence justified. Recording it explicitly is what stops a restriction quietly becoming a re-grant of the wider authority.

attestation.description: The signer's statement, binding them to the exact Passport, conditions and residual risks shown at the moment of signing. An approval that floats free of its evidence is a signature on a blank page.

cryptographically_signed.description: Always false in v0.1. The digest is tamper-evident, not cryptographic: it detects an altered record but does not prove authorship, and anyone able to write the record can recompute it. Stated on the schema rather than left for a reader to discover, because a field that appears to prove provenance and does not is worse than one that admits its limits.
